title: Tests of Dependence: Contingency, ANOVA, Correlation & Regression
sub: Lecture 11 · Seminar 12 · independence test, ANOVA, correlation test, t-test of the slope, linear trend
blurb: Chi-square independence test in contingency tables, one-way ANOVA F-test, correlation test, t-test of the regression slope with causal interpretation, and the linear trend test.
lede: The same five steps as in Seminar 11, applied to relationships: are two categorical variables independent, do group means differ, are two numeric variables correlated, and does the regression line or trend really have a slope?
six: Contingency table: n′ = row total × column total / n, g ≈ χ²((r − 1)(c − 1)), right tail.
The independence test needs **all expected frequencies large enough**; combine categories if not.
ANOVA: H0 μ1 = … = μk, f = [ss<sub>TR</sub>/(k − 1)] / [ss<sub>E</sub>/(n − k)], **F(k − 1, n − k)**.
Correlation test: t = r√(n − 2)/√(1 − r²), **t(n − 2)**, two-tailed.
Slope test: t = b1 / s(b1), **t(n − 2)**; H0 β1 = 0 means no linear relationship.
Inferential slope interpretation is **causal**: +1 unit of x → +b1 units of y **on average**.
must: Independence test, ANOVA and the t-test of the slope

questions.answer: The two variables are linearly independent
questions.e: ρ = 0 means no linear dependence in the population.

questions.q: What does H0: β1 = 0 mean in the t-test of the slope?
questions.answer: There is no linear relationship between x and y
wrong: The line goes through the origin
questions.e: A zero slope means y does not change linearly with x.

questions.q: b1 = 13.802 and s(b1) = 4.354. Value of the test statistic?
b1 = 0.526 for weight (kg) on height (cm). Inferential interpretation?
questions.answer: If height increases by 1 cm, weight increases by 0.526 kg on average
wrong: 52.6 % of weight is explained by height
Every student weighs 0.526 kg per cm
questions.e: The slope is the average change in y for a 1-unit increase in x (causal interpretation).

questions.answer: About 94.9 % of the variability of y is explained by the regression line
wrong: 94.9 % of observations lie on the line
questions.e: The coefficient of determination is the share of explained variability.

questions.q: In the linear trend test, what does H0: β1 = 0 mean?
questions.answer: The data-generating process is the constant trend
questions.e: Zero slope over time = constant trend.

questions.q: Is the choice of magazine related to education (counts in a table)? Which test?
questions.e: Two categorical variables in a contingency table → chi-square independence test.

vocab.meaning: A table of counts n(ij) for two categorical variables with r rows and c columns.
Chi-square test of H0 that two categorical variables are independent; df = (r − 1)(c − 1).
n′(ij) = row total × column total / n: the count expected if the variables were independent.
F-test of H0 that k population means are equal.
ss(TR): variability of the group means around the overall mean; df = k − 1.
ss(E): variability inside the groups; df = n − k.
Distribution of the ANOVA test statistic, F(k − 1, n − k); quantiles in Table V.
Test of H0: ρ = 0 with t = r√(n − 2)/√(1 − r²), T ~ t(n − 2).
ρ(XY): linear dependence of X and Y in the population; estimated by r.
The assumed model Y = β0 + β1·x + ε that produced the data.
Test of H0: β1 = 0 with t = b1 / s(b1), T ~ t(n − p); s(b1) only from Excel.
s(b1): how precisely the slope is estimated; taken from Excel.
r²: share of the variability of y explained by the regression line.
Inferential reading of b1: if x increases by 1 unit, y changes by b1 units on average.
t-test of the slope of Y(t) = β0 + β1·t + ε; H0 means the constant trend.

facts: The H0 of the chi-square test of a contingency table says the variables are {independent|dependent|equal|normal}.
A 3 by 4 contingency table gives {6|12|7|11} degrees of freedom.
The test is not justified when expected frequencies are too {small|large|equal|negative}.
One-way ANOVA compares the {means|variances|medians|proportions} of several groups.
The ANOVA test statistic has the {F|t|chi-square|normal} distribution.
The correlation test uses n minus {2|1|0|3} degrees of freedom.
The value of the test statistic of the slope is b1 divided by its {standard error|variance|mean|intercept}.
The inferential interpretation of the slope is {causal|descriptive|seasonal|random}.
The share of variability explained by the line is the coefficient of {determination|correlation|variation|contingency}.
In the linear trend test, H0 means the {constant|quadratic|seasonal|exponential} trend.
